newsitem.title: GERMANY: German president to stress close ties with France.
newsitem.headline: German president to stress close ties with France.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog pays an official visit to France from Wednesday to Saturday aimed at underlining how close relations are between the two neighbours at the heart of the campaign for a more united Europe.
"We want to stress the normality of French-German friendship," Herzog told journalists in Bonn on Tuesday.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl and President Jacques Chirac meet regularly to coordinate policies to foster closer integration within the European Union.
Herzog, who in contrast to Chirac has a largely ceremonial post, plans to divide his time between Paris and Bordeaux, where Prime Minister Alain Juppe is mayor.

The high point of his stay in Bordeaux will be a visit to Chateau de La Brede, the birthplace of the French political theorist Montesquieu, and a discussion there among French and German intellectuals about the 18th century philosopher's contribution to European thought.
Chirac will be Herzog's guest at a dinner on Thursday in Paris and Juppe will host a dinner in Herzog's honour in Bordeaux after they visit the city hall bombed by Corsican separatists last week.

While in Paris, Herzog plans to open an exhibition about Berlin at la Defense and hold talks with National Assembly President Philippe Seguin, Senate president Rene Monory, UDF party leader Francois Leotard, Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin and Paris Mayor Jean Tiberi.
He will also meet Jewish community leader Jean Kahn and visit the Grand Synagogue of Paris.
Herzog, a Bavarian Christian Democrat and former chief justice of Germany's Federal Constitutional Court, has been president since 1994.
